answer: One person, one scuba diving certification: the certifying agency signs a dive-log attestation binding the diver to a numbered card, issued only after a supervised open-water test. An echo of fake accounts collapses because each forged certificate needs a complicit instructor, a pool session, and a paid exam, roughly $400 and a day of a real human's time per identity. The quartz in this check is the registry lookup: card, logbook, and instructor signature must all match, and any vine of duplicate cards sharing one instructor gets revoked.
